question: With which neighbouring country does India share most of the western border?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India shares most of its **western border** with** Pakistan.**
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is about **3,323 km long** and is known as the** Line of Control (LoC).**
 
• India and Pakistan have a long-standing territorial dispute over the region of **Jammu and Kashmir**, which has led to several conflicts and tensions between the two countries.
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is **heavily guarded** by both sides and is considered to be one of the** most militarized borders **in the world.
 
• The **Wagah border** crossing, located near the city of Amritsar in India and Lahore in Pakistan, is the only road border crossing between the two countries and is a **popular tourist attraction.**
 
• **Myanmar, Bhutan, and China** are India's other neighbouring countries, with whom it shares its **eastern, northern, and northeastern borders**, respectively.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myanmar** (formerly known as Burma) is a **Southeast Asian **country that shares a** 1,643 km** long border with India.

 
 
• The border between India and Myanmar is known as the** Indo-Myanmar border **and is located in the** northeastern states **of India.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan** is a small landlocked country located in the** eastern Himalayas,** which shares a** 699 km long** border with India.
 
 
• The border between India and Bhutan is known as the** Bhutan-India border **and is located in the northeastern states of India.
 
 
 
• **China** is a neighbouring country located in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, which shares a** 3,488 km long** border with India.
 
 
• The border between India and China is known as the** Line of Actual Control (LAC) **and is located in the northeastern states of India.
 
• India and China have a longstanding territorial dispute over the** region of Arunachal Pradesh,** which has led to several conflicts and tensions between the two countries.
